items.title: Systems of imprimitivity for a Borel $G$-space
items.statement: Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological group acting measurably on a standard Borel space $X$ (the map $(g,x)\mapsto gx$ is $\mathcal B(G)\otimes\mathcal B(X)$-measurable), and let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space. A **system of imprimitivity** for the action is a pair $(U,P)$ in which $U:G\to U(H)$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation and $P$ is a projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $X$ such that $U_gP(E)U_g^{-1}=P(gE)$ for every $g\in G$ and every Borel $E\subseteq X$. The family of $P$-null Borel sets is the null-set class of the system; the system is **ergodic** when every Borel $E$ with $U_gP(E)U_g^{-1}=P(E)$ for all $g$ satisfies $P(E)=0$ or $P(E)=I$, and is nonzero when $P(X)=I$ and $H\ne\{0\}$.
items.strategy: The definition names the covariance datum classified by Mackey. Its well-definedness is the projection-valued-measure class of the published PVM definition, together with the requirement that the $G$-action be measurable. The ergodicity clause is the $P$-formulation of ergodicity of the action on the base and is equivalent, for a P-faithful measure, to the usual null-or-conull condition; no topological condition beyond measurability of the action is imposed, and $P$ is not assumed to be regular.

references.title: G. W. Mackey, Imprimitivity for Representations of Locally Compact Groups I, PNAS 35 (1949) 537-545 (Internet Archive capture of the PubMed Central scan)
G. Misra, E. K. Narayanan and C. Varughese, Mackey Imprimitivity and commuting tuples of homogeneous normal operators, arXiv:2402.15737

items.title: The transformation (covariance) algebra $C_c(G\times X)$
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological group acting continuously on a locally compact Hausdorff space $X$, with left Haar measure $dg$ and modular function $\Delta_G$. The **transformation algebra** of the action is the complex vector space $C_c(G\times X)$ of continuous complex functions with compact support, equipped with the twisted convolution $$(f_1*f_2)(g,x)=\int_G f_1(h,x)\,f_2(h^{-1}g,h^{-1}x)\,dh$$ and the involution $f^*(g,x)=\Delta_G(g)^{-1}\overline{f(g^{-1},g^{-1}x)}$. The formulas define a complex associative algebra with involution; when the action is trivial the formula is convolution in the group variable with pointwise multiplication in the base variable.
items.strategy: Use the target-variable convention in the statement. The first factor restricts h to a compact group set and x to a compact base set; the second restricts $h^{-1}g$ to a compact group set. Thus convolution has compact support inside the product of the two group projections and the first base projection. Near any (g,x), uniform continuity on compact parameter sets and a common compact h-support justify continuity of the integral. Both associative expansions are the double integral of $f_1(h,x)f_2(r,h^{-1}x)f_3(r^{-1}h^{-1}g,r^{-1}h^{-1}x)$ after the left-Haar substitution k=hr, proving associativity. For the involution, double application gives f by $\Delta(g^{-1})=\Delta(g)^{-1}$; expanding $f_2^**f_1^*$ combines the modular factors into $\Delta(g)^{-1}$, and substituting r=gh gives exactly $(f_1*f_2)^*(g,x)$. The support transforms by the continuous map $(g,x)\mapsto(g^{-1},g^{-1}x)$, so remains compact. These computations prove the algebra and star identities rather than importing them from a source. AC is inherited through the published compactly supported kernel theorem used to commute the Radon integrals in the associativity argument; no additional independent choice step is claimed.

references.title: M. A. Rieffel, Induced representations of C*-algebras, Advances in Math. 13 (1974) 176-257, §1 (covariance algebras)
V. S. Sunder, Notes on the Imprimitivity Theorem (ISIBangalore/IMSc lecture notes, 22 pp.)

items.title: Characters of the L1 algebra of an abelian group
items.statement:
Assume AC. For a second-countable LCH abelian group $N$ with Haar measure,
every nonzero complex-linear multiplicative functional $\lambda$ on $L^1(N)$
is uniquely $\lambda(f)=\int_N f(n)\chi(n)\,dn$ for a continuous unitary
character $\chi$. This bijection from $\widehat N$ with its compact-open
topology to the character space with its pointwise-evaluation topology is a
homeomorphism. No Pontryagin duality or Fourier inversion theorem is assumed.
items.strategy: Unitization bounds λ by the L1 norm. Abelian translations and the Bochner convolution identity construct χ and its classification formula; bounded powers and inverse powers force modulus one. Positive cutoffs give nonzero converse characters. Compact-open convergence controls integrals, and the compact translation orbit finite-net estimate with both denominator-error and nonvanishing bounds proves inverse continuity.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, An Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, §34A–34C, printed pp. 134–137

items.title: Direct integrals transport along bimeasurable base isomorphisms
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(X,\mathcal B_X,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B_Y,
u)$ be sigma-finite standard Borel measure spaces, let $c:X	o Y$ be a bimeasurable bijection with $
u=c_*\mu$, and let $(H_y)_{y\in Y}$ be a measurable complex Hilbert field over $(Y,
u)$ with direct integral $\int_Y^\oplus H_y\,d
u(y)$. Then $x\mapsto H_{c(x)}$ is a measurable Hilbert field over $(X,\mu)$ with the pulled-back fundamental family, and pullback of sections $\xi\mapsto\xi\circ c$ is a unitary $$c^*:\int_Y^\oplus H_y\,d
u(y)\longrightarrow\int_X^\oplus H_{c(x)}\,d\mu(x)$$ that intertwines multiplication by $f\in L^\infty(Y,
u)$ with multiplication by $f\circ c$. A decomposable operator field $(T_y)$ over $Y$ corresponds to the decomposable field $x\mapsto T_{c(x)}$ over $X$ with the same essential norm and the same fibrewise adjoint and product identities.
items.strategy: Pull back the countable fundamental family: $(e_n\circ c)(x):=e_n(c(x))$ has Borel Gram coefficients because $c$ and the original coefficients are Borel, and its span is dense in every fibre. A section $\xi$ over $Y$ is measurable iff all $\langle\xi(y),e_n(y)\rangle$ are Borel, equivalently $\xi\circ c$ is measurable for the pulled-back field. The change-of-variables formula for the pushforward measure gives equality of the integrated squared norms; surjectivity and the inverse follow by applying the same construction to $c^{-1}$. Intertwining with multiplication is pointwise. The operator-field statement is fibrewise plus the fact that essential suprema are preserved under a measure-space isomorphism.

references.title: J. Dixmier, Von Neumann Algebras, Chapter II §1 (direct integrals and measurable fields)
G. Misra, E. K. Narayanan and C. Varughese, Mackey Imprimitivity and commuting tuples of homogeneous normal operators, arXiv:2402.15737

items.title: Nondegenerate representations of C0 have regular PVMs
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X$ be LCH and $T:C_0(X)\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ a
nondegenerate star representation. Then a unique regular PVM $P$ on $X$ with
$P(X)=I$ satisfies $T(f)=\int_X f\,dP$ for every $f\in C_0(X)$. The zero
Hilbert space has the zero PVM.
items.strategy: Handle the zero Hilbert space separately, then extend T unitaly to C(X+) and apply the compact regular-PVM theorem. Nondegeneracy kills the projection at infinity. Restriction gives the required regular PVM; a competing regular PVM extends by zero, with compact inner approximation in X and complement outer approximation in X+, so compact uniqueness proves uniqueness.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, An Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, §34A–34C, printed pp. 134–137

items.title: Second-countable locally compact Hausdorff spaces are Polish, and homogeneous quotients are standard Borel
items.statement: Assume AC. Every second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space is Polish, hence standard Borel. Consequently, if $G$ is a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological group and $H\le G$ is a closed subgroup, then the homogeneous space $G/H$ with its quotient topology is Polish and the quotient Borel structure together with the left action $G\times G/H\to G/H$ is a standard Borel $G$-space with Borel action.
items.strategy: Second countability gives a countable base of open sets with compact closure; their closures cover $X$, so $X$ is sigma-compact. The space is regular, so Urysohn metrization applies; and a locally compact Hausdorff space is Cech-complete, so metrizability plus Cech-completeness gives complete metrizability. A completely metrizable space is Polish exactly when it is second countable. For the quotient: the quotient map is continuous and open, so images of a countable base form a countable base for $G/H$; $G/H$ is locally compact Hausdorff, and the left action is induced by continuous multiplication, hence is Borel. The empty-space case is vacuous and no further choice is used.

references.title: G. B. Folland, A Course in Abstract Harmonic Analysis, Chapter 2 (locally compact groups and homogeneous spaces, Polish structure)
G. Misra, E. K. Narayanan and C. Varughese, Mackey Imprimitivity and commuting tuples of homogeneous normal operators, arXiv:2402.15737

items.title: Steinhaus and Pettis: Borel homomorphisms of second-countable locally compact groups are continuous
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological
group with left Haar measure $\mu$. (i) If $A\subseteq G$ is Borel with
$0<\mu(A)<\infty$, then $AA^{-1}$ contains an open neighbourhood of the
identity. (ii) If $T$ is a second-countable topological group and
$\varphi:G\to T$ is a Borel-measurable group homomorphism, then $\varphi$ is
continuous. In particular, a Borel homomorphism from a second-countable
locally compact group into the unitary group $U(K)$ of a separable Hilbert
space, with the strong operator topology, is strongly continuous.
items.strategy: For (i), L2 translation continuity applied to $\mathbf1_A$ makes $g\mapsto\langle L_g\mathbf1_A,\mathbf1_A\rangle=\mu(gA\cap A)$ continuous, with value $\mu(A)>0$ at e. Therefore $gA\cap A\ne\varnothing$ in an identity neighborhood, so $g\in AA^{-1}$. For (ii), take a symmetric identity neighborhood V of T with $V^2\subset U$. The subspace $\varphi(G)$ is second countable and hence Lindelof, so its cover by $\varphi(g)V\cap\varphi(G)$ has a countable subcover with centers $\varphi(g_n)$ actually in the image. If $\varphi^{-1}(V)$ were null then the sets $g_n\varphi^{-1}(V)$ would cover G by null sets, contradicting positivity of Haar. Thus the preimage has positive measure; intersect it with a compact exhaustion to obtain a positive finite-measure Borel subset A. By (i), an identity neighborhood lies in $AA^{-1}\subset\varphi^{-1}(V^2)\subset\varphi^{-1}(U)$, proving continuity at e and hence everywhere. For separable K the strong unitary topology is metrized by the actions on a countable orthonormal basis; U(K) embeds in the countable product of the separable metric spaces K, so it is second countable.

references.title: A. Putman, Lie groups and automatic continuity, proof of Pettis theorem via Steinhaus, pp. 1-2
V. S. Sunder, Notes on the Imprimitivity Theorem (ISIBangalore/IMSc lecture notes, 22 pp.)

items.title: Unitary intertwiners preserve fibre multiplicity over a standard Borel base
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X$ be a standard Borel space, $\mu$ a nonzero finite Borel
measure on $X$, and let $m,m':X\to\{1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ be Borel
multiplicity functions. If there is a unitary
$$U:L^2(X,\mu;m)\longrightarrow L^2(X,\mu;m')$$
with $UM_f=M_fU$ for every bounded Borel $f:X\to\mathbb C$, then $m=m'$
$\mu$-almost everywhere. Consequently a multiplicity model of a
projection-valued measure over a fixed base is unique in multiplicity, and a
unitary intertwiner of two such models is a decomposable operator whose fibres
are unitary almost everywhere.
items.strategy: Localize to the Borel pieces $B_{k,k'}=\{m=k\}\cap\{m'=k'\}$ for constants $k,k'\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$; the indicator of a piece commutes with $U$ and the pieces form a countable partition, so each positive-measure piece carries a unitary between constant-fibre models $\bigoplus_{r\le k}L^2(\mu|_B)$ and $\bigoplus_{s\le k'}L^2(\mu|_B)$ commuting with all multiplications. The commutant of the diagonal multiplications on a constant-fibre model consists of matrices of multiplication operators, and testing on coordinate vectors turns the matrix of multipliers into a fibrewise linear isometry of $\ell^2(k)$ into $\ell^2(k')$; the adjoint identities make it onto, forcing $k=k'$. At most countably many pieces, so the union of the unequal positive-measure pieces is null; hence $m=m'$ a.e. This is the standard-base form of the constant-fibre rigidity used in the separable spectral multiplicity theory.

references.title: J. B. Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis, 2nd ed., Chapter IX §10, Propositions 10.17-10.19 (multiplicity rigidity)
G. Misra, E. K. Narayanan and C. Varughese, Mackey Imprimitivity and commuting tuples of homogeneous normal operators, arXiv:2402.15737

items.title: A system of imprimitivity integrates to a nondegenerate representation of the transformation algebra
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(U,P)$ be a system of imprimitivity on a second-countable
locally compact Hausdorff $G$-space $X$ with continuous action, as required by
the transformation-algebra definition. For $f\in C_c(G\times X)$ define
$\pi(f)$ by the scalar pairing
$$\langle\pi(f)\xi,\eta\rangle=\int_G\int_X f(g,x)\,dE_{U_g\xi,\eta}(x)\,dg\qquad(\xi,\eta\in H),$$
where $E_{\xi,\eta}(B)=\langle P(B)\xi,\eta\rangle$. Then $\pi(f)$ is a
bounded operator,
$\|\pi(f)\|\le\int_G\|f(g,\cdot)\|_\infty\,dg$, the map $f\mapsto\pi(f)$ is a
$\ast$-representation of the transformation algebra $C_c(G\times X)$, and it
is nondegenerate: the closed span of $\pi(C_c(G\times X))H$ is $H$.
items.strategy: For fixed g, let $M_{f(g,\cdot)}=\int f(g,x)dP(x)$. For each vector, $g\mapsto M_{f(g,\cdot)}U_g\xi$ is strongly continuous and compactly supported: near g the functions f(g,.) vary uniformly on a common compact base set. Its Bochner integral defines pi, with the displayed norm bound. Covariance gives $U_h M_b=M_{b\circ h^{-1}}U_h$, so expanding the product and applying Bochner/Fubini yields $\pi(f_1)\pi(f_2)=\int\!\int M_{f_1(h,x)f_2(r,h^{-1}x)}U_{hr}\,dh\,dr=\pi(f_1*f_2)$ after the left-Haar substitution g=hr. The adjoint identity follows from $U_g^*M_{\overline{f(g,\cdot)}}=M_{\overline{f(g,g\,\cdot)}}U_{g^{-1}}$ and Haar inversion, giving the stated modular involution. For nondegeneracy, choose $0\le b_n\le1$ in Cc(X) with b_n tending pointwise to 1, from a compact exhaustion and cutoff lemma; bounded PVM dominated convergence gives $M_{b_n}\to I$ strongly. Choose the published nonnegative norm-one group approximate identity a_i supported near e; strong continuity gives $U(a_i)\to I$. Then $\pi(a_i\otimes b_n)=M_{b_n}U(a_i)$ approximates every vector by first choosing n and then i. Thus the closed span of pi(Cc)H is H. The selected homogeneous-space case X=G/H satisfies every added topological hypothesis.

references.title: G. W. Mackey, Imprimitivity for Representations of Locally Compact Groups I, PNAS 35 (1949) 537-545 (Internet Archive capture of the PubMed Central scan)
V. S. Sunder, Notes on the Imprimitivity Theorem (ISIBangalore/IMSc lecture notes, 22 pp.)

items.title: Borel cross-sections for closed subgroups of second-countable groups
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological
group, $H\le G$ a closed subgroup, and $q:G\to G/H$ the quotient map. Then
there is a Borel cross-section $s:G/H\to G$ with $q\circ s=\mathrm{id}_{G/H}$,
and for every $g\in G$ there is a unique $h(g,x)\in H$ with
$g\,s(x)=s(gx)\,h(g,x)$, where $x\in G/H$; the map
$(g,x)\mapsto h(g,x)$ is Borel into $H$. Consequently the map
$G\to G/H\times H$, $g\mapsto(q(g),s(q(g))^{-1}g)$, is a Borel isomorphism onto
$G/H\times H$, and the quasi-invariant measure class on $G/H$ may be
transported to a $\sigma$-finite measure on $G$ along $s$.
items.strategy: A least-index recursion through relatively compact basic sets of decreasing diameter selects a Borel Cauchy sequence in each coset. Its limit is a Borel section by distance tests and continuity of q. The section image is a Borel fixed-point set; its pushforward measure is carried by that image and is σ-finite. Exact section cocycle and mutually inverse Borel product coordinates follow from group operations.

references.title: V. S. Sunder, Notes on the Imprimitivity Theorem (ISIBangalore/IMSc lecture notes, 22 pp.)
G. Misra, E. K. Narayanan and C. Varughese, Mackey Imprimitivity and commuting tuples of homogeneous normal operators, arXiv:2402.15737
G. W. Mackey, Induced representations of locally compact groups I, Ann. of Math. 55 (1952) 101-139 (Borel sections of homogeneous spaces)

items.title: LCA Fourier transforms form a dense algebra in C0 of the dual
items.statement:
Assume AC and let $N$ be a second-countable LCH abelian group. With
$\widehat f(\chi)=\int_Nf(n)\chi(n)\,dn$, each $f\in L^1(N)$ has
$\widehat f\in C_0(\widehat N)$, and the functions $\widehat f$ form a
self-adjoint separating nowhere-vanishing algebra whose uniform closure is
$C_0(\widehat N)$. No injectivity or inversion claim is needed.
items.strategy: The compact character space of the L1 unitization is the dual plus augmentation. Continuous evaluation vanishes at augmentation, so its positive superlevel sets are compact subsets of the dual. Convolution/involution give a self-adjoint algebra; character separation and positive cutoffs give separation and no common zeros. Unital Stone–Weierstrass followed by subtracting the small constant term proves C0 density.

references.title: Lynn H. Loomis, An Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, §34A–34C, printed pp. 134–137

items.title: Multiplicity model of a projection-valued measure over a standard Borel base
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X$ be a standard Borel space, $P$ a projection-valued measure
on $X$ acting on a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, and let $\mu$
be a finite Borel measure on $X$ that is $P$-faithful, i.e. $P(E)=0$ iff
$\mu(E)=0$. Then there exist a Borel function
$m:X\to\{1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ and a unitary
$$W:H\longrightarrow\int_X^\oplus\mathbb C^{m(x)}\,d\mu(x)$$
such that $WP(E)W^{-1}=M_{\mathbf 1_E}$ for every Borel $E\subseteq X$. Such a
$\mu$ exists for every nonzero separable $H$: for any dense sequence $(\xi_j)$
with $\xi_j\ne0$,
$\mu=\sum_j2^{-j}\|\xi_j\|^{-2}\langle P(\cdot)\xi_j,\xi_j\rangle$ is finite,
$P$-faithful and Borel. Any two $P$-faithful measures are mutually absolutely
continuous.
items.strategy: A normalized dense-vector sum gives a finite faithful measure. Code X into a Borel Y⊂[0,1], form S=∫c dP, and use the bounded resolvent integral to bound its spectrum. The regular pushed PVM equals E_S, so P(B)=E_S(c(B)). Apply the published cyclic spectral-multiplicity construction to the prescribed generator S of the abelian W*(S). Its measure ν and c_*μ have the same null class, rather than necessarily being equal. Restrict/zero-extend on conull σ(S)∩Y, change measure by the RN unitary, and only then pull back through the bijection c:X→Y. Fixed-base rigidity gives multiplicity uniqueness.

references.title: C. Anantharaman and S. Popa, An Introduction to II_1 Factors, Chapter 8 §8.1 (spectral multiplicity model)
G. Misra, E. K. Narayanan and C. Varughese, Mackey Imprimitivity and commuting tuples of homogeneous normal operators, arXiv:2402.15737
V. S. Sunder, Notes on the Imprimitivity Theorem (ISIBangalore/IMSc lecture notes, 22 pp.)

items.title: Ergodic systems with regular orbits concentrate on one orbit
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(U,P)$ be an ergodic system of imprimitivity for a Borel action
of a group $G$ on a standard Borel space $X$, acting on a nonzero separable
Hilbert space, and suppose the orbit equivalence relation of the action is
**regular**: there is a countable family $E_1,E_2,\dots$ of $G$-invariant
Borel subsets of $X$ such that every orbit is the intersection of the sets
$E_n$ that contain it. Equivalently, some countable family of invariant Borel
sets separates distinct orbits, which is the condition that the orbit space is
countably separated. Then there is an orbit $C\subseteq X$ with
$P(X\setminus C)=0$.
items.strategy: Ergodicity makes each invariant projection $P(E_n)$ either zero or I. Put $F_n=E_n$ in the latter case and $F_n=X\setminus E_n$ in the former. Then $P(F_n)=I$ for every n. The complements have zero scalar measure for every vector; countable additivity implies $P(C)=I$ for $C=\bigcap_nF_n$. Since the Hilbert space is nonzero, C is nonempty. Pick x in C. Its orbit lies in C because the F_n are invariant; conversely any y in C belongs to every E_n containing x, so the regularity hypothesis puts y in the orbit of x. Thus C is exactly one orbit and is Borel as the countable intersection. No assertion that the countable Boolean algebra has countably many nonempty atoms is needed; its signature classes may be uncountable.

references.title: G. W. Mackey, Imprimitivity for Representations of Locally Compact Groups I, PNAS 35 (1949) 537-545 (Internet Archive capture of the PubMed Central scan)
V. S. Sunder, Notes on the Imprimitivity Theorem (ISIBangalore/IMSc lecture notes, 22 pp.)

items.title: Haar null classes and Borel descent on a homogeneous space
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be second-countable LCH, $H$ closed, $q:G\to G/H$, and $s$
a Borel section. Every nonzero $\sigma$-finite quasi-invariant Borel measure
$\mu$ on $G/H$ is equivalent to a rho-derived quotient measure. The coordinates
$(x,h)\mapsto s(x)h$ carry the product quotient/Haar measure class to the Haar
measure class on $G$. In particular $\mu(E)=0$ iff $q^{-1}(E)$ is Haar null. If
a Borel map $F:G/H\times H\to U(K)$ for separable $K$ satisfies
$F(x,hk)=F(x,h)$ for every $k$ and almost every $(x,h)$, then
$F(x,h)=B(x)$ almost everywhere for a Borel $B:G/H\to U(K)$.
items.strategy: Compact cutoff bounds and second-countable Borel regularity license RMK uniqueness to extend Weil to Borel sets. Thus product section coordinates push quotient/Haar measure to ρ dt and preserve null classes. Averaging an equivalent probability against positive Haar density proves uniqueness of the nonzero σ-finite quasi-invariant base class. Tonelli and (h,k)→(h,hk) force right-invariant fields constant on almost every H fibre; coefficient averaging selects the Borel descended unitary.

references.title: G. W. Mackey, Imprimitivity for Representations of Locally Compact Groups I, PNAS 35 (1949) 537-545 (Internet Archive capture of the PubMed Central scan)

items.title: Spectral measure of a unitary representation of an abelian group, covariance, and ergodicity
items.statement:
Assume AC, and let $N$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff abelian
group, $\pi:N\to U(\mathcal H)$ a strongly continuous unitary representation on
a separable Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, and $K$ a second-countable locally
compact group acting continuously on $N$ by automorphisms $\alpha_k$, with dual
action $k\cdot\chi=\chi\circ\alpha_k^{-1}$ on $\widehat N$. If
$\tau:K\to U(\mathcal H)$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation with
$\tau(k)\pi(n)\tau(k)^{-1}=\pi(\alpha_k(n))$, then there is a unique regular
projection-valued measure $P$ on $\widehat N$ with
$$\pi(n)=\int_{\widehat N}\chi(n)\,dP(\chi)\quad(n\in N),\qquad \tau(k)P(E)\tau(k)^{-1}=P(k\cdot E)$$
for every Borel $E\subseteq\widehat N$. If in addition the representation
$n\mapsto\pi(n)$, $k\mapsto\tau(k)$ of $N\rtimes K$ is irreducible, then the
measure class of $P$ is ergodic for the action of $K$ on $\widehat N$: every
Borel $E$ with $P(E)$ invariant under $\tau$ satisfies $P(E)=0$ or $P(E)=I$.
items.strategy: First derive L1 separability from scalar L2 separability by finite compact and bounded-value truncations; countable dense evaluations then prove dual second countability. Integrate π on L1 and use an approximate identity for nondegeneracy. Gelfand characters give the uniform Fourier norm bound, so Fourier density extends to a nondegenerate C0 representation and hence a regular PVM. Construct R(n) from this PVM, prove continuity by dominated convergence, and use jointly continuous evaluation/Fubini plus positive cutoffs to show R=π. Regular uniqueness gives covariance; irreducibility makes invariant spectral projections trivial. Handle H=0 separately.

references.title: V. S. Sunder, Notes on the Imprimitivity Theorem (ISIBangalore/IMSc lecture notes, 22 pp.)
D. P. Williams, Lecture Notes on the Spectral Theorem, Example 3.10, printed p. 9
B. Bekka and P. de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters, arXiv:1912.07262 (AMS Mathematical Surveys and Monographs 250)
Lynn H. Loomis, An Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, §34A–34C, printed pp. 134–137

items.title: Transitive systems of imprimitivity and their normalized measure class
items.statement: A system of imprimitivity $(U,P)$ on a standard Borel $G$-space $X$ is **transitive** when $X$ is $G$-equivariantly isomorphic to a homogeneous space $G/H$ with $H\le G$ closed, the isomorphism carrying the Borel structure of $G/H$ (hence then $G$ is second-countable locally compact, the action on $G/H$ is the left-coset action, and the stabilizer of the identity coset is $H$). For a transitive system one fixes the base identification $X=G/H$. Assume AC for the following normalized-measure existence and uniqueness assertions: a **normalized representative** is a strongly quasi-invariant Radon measure $\mu_\rho$ on $G/H$ built from a rho-function $\rho$. The normalized homogeneous measure class is the unique class of nonzero quasi-invariant Radon measures on $G/H$; the system is called transitive on $G/H$.
items.strategy: The equivariant Borel coset-space condition defines transitivity without invoking choice or a classification theorem. AC is needed for the asserted normalized-measure supply: existence is the published rho-function theorem, and uniqueness of the nonzero sigma-finite quasi-invariant class is the proved local Haar-lift lemma, not an unstated uniqueness clause of the existence theorem. Different rho-functions give representatives in this class. The identity-coset stabilizer is H by the explicit coset computation. Consumers that use only the definitional term transitive do not consume the normalized-measure existence assertion.

references.title: G. W. Mackey, Imprimitivity for Representations of Locally Compact Groups I, PNAS 35 (1949) 537-545 (Internet Archive capture of the PubMed Central scan)
V. S. Sunder, Notes on the Imprimitivity Theorem (ISIBangalore/IMSc lecture notes, 22 pp.)

items.title: A transitive Borel $G$-space with a quasi-invariant measure class is ergodic
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological group, $H\le G$ a closed subgroup, and $\mu$ a nonzero quasi-invariant Radon measure on $G/H$. If $E\subseteq G/H$ is Borel with $\mu(E\,\triangle\,gE)=0$ for every $g\in G$, then $\mu(E)=0$ or $\mu((G/H)\setminus E)=0$. Equivalently, any transitive system of imprimitivity on $G/H$ whose measure class is the quasi-invariant class is ergodic.
items.strategy: Lift the invariant Borel indicator to G using the quotient null-class equivalence. Sigma-finite Tonelli reverses the iterated integral of |f(gt)-f(t)| and supplies a t_0 with equality for almost every g. Right translation of its exceptional null set gives f(u)=f(t_0) for almost every u. The quotient null equivalence gives null or conull E. The PVM intersection law gives the system assertion.

references.title: G. W. Mackey, Imprimitivity for Representations of Locally Compact Groups I, PNAS 35 (1949) 537-545 (Internet Archive capture of the PubMed Central scan)
G. B. Folland, A Course in Abstract Harmonic Analysis, Chapter 2 §2.6 (transitive quasi-invariant actions are ergodic)

items.title: Haar regularization of transitive unitary cocycles
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G,H,\mu,s$ be as in the Haar-lift lemma, $K$ separable, and
$c:G\times G/H\to U(K)$ Borel with
$c(g_1g_2,x)=c(g_1,g_2x)c(g_2,x)$ for each pair and almost every $x$. Suppose
$g\mapsto c(g,\cdot)$ is continuous in local convergence in measure in the
strong topology of $U(K)$. Then there exist a strongly continuous unitary
representation $\sigma:H\to U(K)$ and a Borel $B:G/H\to U(K)$ with
$c(g,x)=B(gx)\sigma(s(gx)^{-1}gs(x))B(x)^{-1}$ for every $g$ and almost every
$x$. This formula gives a strict Borel cocycle on all of $G\times G/H$. The
representation $\sigma$ is unique up to unitary equivalence under Borel
changes of fibre gauge.
items.strategy: Lift the cocycle law to Haar triples, select w0 by Fubini, and factor c(g,q(t))=b(gt)b(t)^{-1} for almost every (g,t). RN truncation of q_*(1_C dt) transfers local-measure continuity to the lift; translation continuity and finite-vector approximation through b(t)^{-1} upgrade to each fixed g. Right-H ratios are left-invariant and hence constant; coefficient averaging makes σ Borel and Pettis makes it continuous. Borel descent gives B. Exact section cocycle gives strict factorization. Two lifts differ by a constant unitary, proving gauge-invariant equivalence of σ.

items.title: Unitary equivalence of systems of imprimitivity and of the induced representations
items.statement: Two systems of imprimitivity $(U,P)$ on $H$ and $(U',P')$ on $H'$ for the same Borel $G$-space $X$ are **unitarily equivalent** when there is a unitary $W:H\to H'$ with $WU_gW^{-1}=U'_g$ and $WP(E)W^{-1}=P'(E)$ for every $g\in G$ and Borel $E\subseteq X$; if both are transitive on $X=G/H$, such a $W$ is called an equivalence of transitive systems. Two strongly continuous unitary representations $\sigma,\sigma'$ of a common group are unitarily equivalent when there is a unitary intertwiner between them.
items.strategy: A definition: the equivalence relation is the natural isomorphism of pairs (representation, projection-valued measure), and its restriction to transitive systems is compared with unitary equivalence of the inducing representations in the uniqueness theorem. No confusion arises from suppressing the base isomorphism in the notation because the transitive case fixes $X=G/H$; the unitarity of $W$ makes the relation symmetric and transitive.

items.title: An induced representation carries a canonical system of imprimitivity on $G/H$
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological
group, $H\le G$ closed, and $\sigma:H\to U(V)$ a strongly continuous unitary
representation on a separable Hilbert space $V$. Let
$\Pi_\sigma=\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\sigma$ be the induced representation on the
covariant completion $\mathcal H_\sigma$ with rho-measure $\mu_\rho$. For a
Borel set $E\subseteq G/H$ define $P(E)$ on the covariant model by
$(P(E)F)(x)=\mathbf 1_E(xH)F(x)$. Then $P$ is a projection-valued measure on
$G/H$, $P(E)$ is well defined on the completed space of measurable covariant
sections, $\Pi_\sigma(g)P(E)\Pi_\sigma(g)^{-1}=P(gE)$ for all $g\in G$ and
Borel $E$, and $(\Pi_\sigma,P)$ is a system of imprimitivity on $G/H$ with
$P(G/H)=I$. If $H=G$ the base is one point and $P(\{G\})=I$; if $H=\{e\}$ one
may normalize so that the system is the multiplication system on $L^2(G;V)$
with the left regular action $F\mapsto F(g^{-1}\,\cdot)$.
items.strategy: On the dense covariant continuous model, multiplication by $\mathbf 1_E$ preserves covariance and is self-adjoint and idempotent; the induced norm is the quotient integral of the pointwise norm, so multiplication by an indicator is a contraction and extends to the completion. Countable additivity follows pointwise from $\mathbf 1_{\sqcup E_n}=\sum_n\mathbf 1_{E_n}$ together with dominated convergence in $L^2$. For covariance insert the explicit action $(\Pi_\sigma(g)F)(x)=D_g(xH)^{1/2}F(g^{-1}x)$ and use $\mathbf 1_E(g^{-1}x)=\mathbf 1_{gE}(x)$. The boundary identifications are clauses of the published induction theorem. No regularity of $P$ beyond the PVM axioms is needed, since $P$ is multiplication defined from the Borel structure.

items.title: Spectral multiplicity model of a transitive system of imprimitivity
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological
group, $H\le G$ a closed subgroup, and let $(U,P)$ be a transitive system of
imprimitivity on $X=G/H$ acting on a nonzero separable Hilbert space $H_0$.
Then there exist a finite Borel measure $\mu$ on $G/H$ in the quasi-invariant
class, a nonzero separable Hilbert space $K$, and a unitary
$$W:H_0\longrightarrow L^2(G/H,\mu;K)$$
such that $WP(E)W^{-1}=M_{\mathbf 1_E}$ for every Borel $E\subseteq G/H$.
Moreover $\mu$ is quasi-invariant under every $g\in G$, and the multiplicity
is constant almost everywhere; any two such normalizations differ by a
decomposable unitary, so $K$ is determined up to isometric isomorphism and
$\mu$ up to equivalence.
items.strategy: Faithful μ0 and covariance give a quasi-invariant multiplicity model. The correctly directed pullback c_g* T_g maps into m∘g over (g^{-1})_*μ0 and intertwines M_f. RN conversion to μ0 permits rigidity, giving m=m∘g almost everywhere for each g. Ergodicity makes one countable multiplicity level conull. Restrict and zero-extend to obtain constant K; common-measure transport and rigidity prove uniqueness.

items.title: Measurable cocycle fields for a multiplicity-normalized system
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(U,P)$ be a transitive system of imprimitivity on $G/H$ and
fix a normalization $W:H_0\to L^2(G/H,\mu;K)$ with
$WP(E)W^{-1}=M_{\mathbf 1_E}$, $G$ second countable locally compact, $H$
closed, $K$ separable, $\mu$ a nonzero $\sigma$-finite quasi-invariant Borel measure. For $g\in G$ let $V_g$ be the
canonical translation operator
$(V_gf)(x)=[d((L_g)_*\mu)/d\mu(x)]^{1/2}f(g^{-1}x)$ and put
$W_g=V_g^{-1}WU_gW^{-1}$. Then $W_g$ commutes with all multiplications and is
therefore multiplication by an essentially bounded measurable operator field
$x\mapsto\varphi_g(x)\in\mathcal B(K)$; the field may be chosen so that
$(g,x)\mapsto\langle\varphi_g(x)\xi,\eta\rangle$ is Borel on $G\times G/H$ for
$\xi,\eta$ in a fixed dense countable subset of $K$ and so that
$\varphi_g(x)$ is unitary for almost every $x$ and every $g$, with the cocycle
identity
$$\varphi_{g_1g_2}(x)=\varphi_{g_1}(g_2x)\,\varphi_{g_2}(x)$$
holding for every $g_1,g_2$ and almost every $x$.
items.strategy: Keep the fixed nonzero σ-finite Borel measure μ. RN transport from a rho measure proves the canonical V_g strongly continuous. Covariance puts W_g=V_g^{-1}T_g in the diagonal commutant before decomposability is invoked. Choose a strictly positive r∈L2(μ); least dense-section approximants to W_g(re_j) with summable squared errors give jointly Borel columns after division by r. Countable convergence, Gram and completeness tests allow identity on the exceptional set, which is null for each fixed g. Tests on 1_E e_j give local-measure continuity. Expanding T and V gives the source-variable pairwise a.e. law. No prescribed null coset is evaluated.

items.title: The stabilizer acts unitarily on an imprimitivity fibre
items.statement:
Assume AC and let $(U,P)$ be a transitive system on $G/H$ on a separable
Hilbert space, with multiplicity-normalized model and source-variable cocycle
fields $\varphi_g$ as above. Fix a Borel section $s$ with $s(eH)=e$. There
exist a Borel unitary field $B_x$ and a strongly continuous unitary
representation $\sigma:H\to U(K)$, unique up to unitary equivalence, such that
for every $g$ and almost every $x$,
$$\varphi_g(x)=B_{gx}\,\sigma(h(g,x))\,B_x^{-1},$$
where $h(g,x)=s(gx)^{-1}gs(x)$. The representatives can be replaced by this
strict formula on all pairs and normalized with $B_{eH}=I$, so that
$\sigma(h)=\varphi_h(eH)$ and $B_x=\varphi_{s(x)}(eH)$. Changes of fields or
section give equivalent $\sigma$. If $H=G$ one recovers the original
representation; if $H$ is trivial the recovered representation is trivial.
items.strategy: Apply Haar regularization to the jointly Borel source cocycle: the cocycle lemma supplies continuity in local measure, and the Haar-lift/descent and regularization lemmas prove every measurable step. They produce B and a strongly continuous sigma with the displayed factorization, without evaluating an a.e. class at eH. Set $s(eH)=e$ by a Borel single-point modification. If the base point is null, set $B_{eH}=I$; for fixed g this modifies the factorization only on $\{eH,g^{-1}eH\}$, both null. If it is an atom, conjugate the entire factorization by $B_{eH}$ to normalize that value. Replace the fields by the strict Borel formula and now, only now, evaluate it at eH to obtain $\varphi_h(eH)=\sigma(h)$ and $\varphi_{s(x)}(eH)=B_x$. The strict section identity verifies the cocycle law everywhere. Uniqueness under a.e. representative or gauge changes is the Haar-Fubini uniqueness argument in the regularization lemma; a change of section changes B by its corresponding sigma factor and leaves the equivalence class fixed. The one-point and trivial-stabilizer cases follow directly from the factorization.

items.title: The imprimitivity reconstruction map is isometric and intertwining
items.statement:
Assume AC. In the normalized model of a transitive system $(U,P)$ on $G/H$,
take the Borel unitaries $B$ and the stabilizer representation $\sigma$
supplied by the preceding lemma. Multiplication by $B$ is unitary and
$$(B^{-1}WU_gW^{-1}Bf)(x)=D_g(x)^{1/2}\sigma(s(x)^{-1}gs(g^{-1}x))f(g^{-1}x).$$
This is the canonical induced action of $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\sigma$.
Moreover $B^{-1}WP(E)W^{-1}B=M_{\mathbf 1_E}$ for all Borel $E$. Hence $(U,P)$
is unitarily equivalent to the canonical induced system by an isometric map
intertwining both $U$ and $P$.
items.strategy: The preceding lemma supplies a Borel unitary B, so its multiplication operator is unitary. The source-variable convention is $WU_gW^{-1}f(x)=D_g(x)^{1/2}\varphi_g(g^{-1}x)f(g^{-1}x)$. Substitute $\varphi_g(g^{-1}x)=B_x\sigma(s(x)^{-1}gs(g^{-1}x))B_{g^{-1}x}^{-1}$ and conjugate by B. The B factors cancel at their respective target and source points, yielding exactly the displayed section form of the published covariant induced representation. Being decomposable, B commutes with scalar multiplication and therefore with all PVM indicators. The induction measure-independence theorem handles the equivalent finite representative. Thus the map is onto, isometric, and intertwines both members of the system.

items.title: Mackey's imprimitivity theorem
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological
group, $H\le G$ a closed subgroup, and $(U,P)$ a transitive system of
imprimitivity on $G/H$ acting on a separable Hilbert space $H_0$. Then there
exist a strongly continuous unitary representation $\sigma:H\to U(K)$ on a
separable Hilbert space $K$ and a unitary
$$W:H_0\longrightarrow L^2(G/H,\mu;K)$$
onto the induced space of $\sigma$ such that
$$WU_gW^{-1}=\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\sigma(g)\quad(g\in G),\qquad WP(E)W^{-1}=M_{\mathbf 1_E}\quad(E\subseteq G/H\ \text{Borel}),$$
where $M_{\mathbf 1_E}$ is multiplication by the indicator of $E$ on the
covariant model. Conversely, for every strongly continuous unitary
$\sigma:H\to U(K)$ on a separable Hilbert space $K$, the induced representation together with multiplication by
indicators on $G/H$ is a transitive system of imprimitivity, and the two
constructions are inverse up to unitary equivalence. The uniqueness theorem
records the corresponding bijection of equivalence classes.
items.strategy: For the zero Hilbert space choose the zero stabilizer fibre and the zero induced system. For a nonzero system, the forward direction assembles the spectral multiplicity model, the cocycle fields and the reconstruction unitary: the model gives the base and the PVM action, the cocycle fields produce the stabilizer representation, and the reconstruction map conjugates the system into the canonical induced system. The reverse direction is the canonical-system lemma. Both directions use the second countability of $G$ through the Borel cross-section and the standard Borel structure of $G/H$, and the separability of the Hilbert spaces through the multiplicity model. No regularity of the PVM is needed once the measure model is fixed, and the statement makes no claim for nontransitive or non-standard orbit spaces.

items.title: Uniqueness in the imprimitivity theorem
items.statement:
Assume AC and keep the hypotheses of the imprimitivity theorem. If
$\sigma:H\to U(K)$ and $\sigma':H\to U(K')$ are strongly continuous unitary
representations, then the canonical transitive systems of
$\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\sigma$ and $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\sigma'$ on $G/H$
are unitarily equivalent if and only if $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ are unitarily
equivalent. Consequently the map of the imprimitivity theorem is a bijection
between unitary equivalence classes of transitive systems on $G/H$ and unitary
equivalence classes of strongly continuous unitary representations of $H$.
items.strategy: An H-intertwining unitary acts fibrewise and intertwines the canonical systems. Conversely a system equivalence intertwines scalar multiplications, so the published commutant and multiplicity-rigidity suppliers make it multiplication by a Borel unitary field A between equal-dimensional fibres. Fix a unitary identification of those fibres. The G-intertwining equation says the source cocycles for sigma and sigma-prime differ by the gauge A. Apply the Haar-Fubini uniqueness proof in the regularization lemma: lifting the gauge to G makes $b_2(t)^{-1}A(q(t))b_1(t)$ left-translation invariant for every g a.e., hence a constant unitary T. Right-H covariance gives $\sigma'(h)T=T\sigma(h)$ for every h. This proves equivalence of the stabilizer representations without evaluating A at a null coset. The two directions give the claimed bijection. Zero fibres induce exactly the zero system; a nonzero fibre induces a nonzero space by the full-support quotient measure and nonzero square-integrable sections, so the zero cases are immediate.

items.title: Mackey little-group reduction for an abelian normal subgroup
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G=N\rtimes K$ be a topological semidirect product with continuous automorphism action and product topology, $N$ abelian and
closed normal, $G$ second countable locally compact, and let the dual action of
$K$ on $\widehat N$ have regular orbits in the sense of the preceding lemma
(equivalently, the orbit space $\widehat N/K$ is countably separated). For
$\chi\in\widehat N$ let $K_\chi=\{k\in K:k\cdot\chi=\chi\}$ and
$H_\chi=N\rtimes K_\chi$. Then every irreducible strongly continuous unitary
representation $\pi$ of $G$ is unitarily equivalent to
$\operatorname{Ind}_{H_\chi}^G(\chi\otimes\theta)$ for some
$\chi\in\widehat N$ and some irreducible strongly continuous unitary
representation $\theta$ of $K_\chi$, where $\chi\otimes\theta$ denotes the
representation $(n,k_\chi)\mapsto\chi(n)\theta(k_\chi)$ of $H_\chi$.
items.strategy: The continuous topological semidirect product supplies the needed LCH groups. A countable dense group orbit of a cyclic nonzero vector proves arbitrary irreducible π separable. Its N spectral PVM is ergodic and regular orbits concentrate it on one Borel orbit. Compact exhaustions of quotient opens prove the continuous orbit bijection inverse Borel. Transport the system to G/Hχ and apply imprimitivity. With section in K, a common conull point for countably many n and strong continuity give σ|N=χI; restrict to Kχ for θ. A nontrivial θ reducing subspace would induce a nonzero proper reducing subspace, proving θ irreducible. This proves exhaustiveness.

items.title: A nontransitive system with two orbits is not classified by one stabilizer
items.statement:
False claim: every system of imprimitivity for a group $G$ is classified, up to
unitary equivalence, by a single closed subgroup $H\le G$ and a strongly
continuous unitary representation of $H$; that is, Mackey's imprimitivity
classification needs no transitivity or ergodicity hypothesis.
items.strategy: For the discrete finite group Z/2, the unitary swap with square I has continuous orbit maps. Its three coordinate projections satisfy covariance. The two invariant orbit summands are nontrivial and separately transitive. A homogeneous Z/2 base has only one or two points and cannot be equivariantly identified with this faithful three-point base.

items.title: The regular translation system on $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$: position, momentum and trivial stabilizer
items.statement:
Assume AC and let $n\ge0$ be an integer. Let $G=\mathbb R^n$ act on $X=\mathbb R^n$ by translation, let
$U=\lambda_G$ be the left regular representation on $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$, and let
$P(E)$ be multiplication by the indicator of a Borel set
$E\subseteq\mathbb R^n$. Then $(U,P)$ is a transitive system of imprimitivity
on $\mathbb R^n=\mathbb R^n/\{0\}$ with trivial stabilizer, $P$ is the joint
spectral measure of the $n$ commuting self-adjoint position operators
$M_{x_j}$ of multiplication by the coordinates, and $U$ is the representation
induced from the trivial representation of the trivial subgroup; the
momentum operators are the self-adjoint Fourier multipliers $P_j=\mathcal F_2^{-1}M_{2\pi\xi_j}\mathcal F_2$ on $D_j=\{f\in L^2:\xi_j\mathcal F_2f\in L^2\}$, with $U_{te_j}=e^{-itP_j}$. With the repository convention $U_{te_j}=e^{itT_j}$, the full self-adjoint and derivative generators are $T_j=-P_j$ and $G_j=-iP_j$ on $D_j$. On Schwartz functions, $P_j=-i\partial_j$, $T_j=i\partial_j$ and $G_j=-\partial_j$; the differential notation here is asserted on that test space. The system is the classical model behind the
imprimitivity theorem and behind the position-momentum form of the
Stone-von Neumann uniqueness theorem.
items.strategy: Treat n=0 as the unit-mass singleton with zero metric and no coordinates. For n≥1, direct translation covariance gives P(E+t), and trivial-subgroup induction identifies the system. Real coordinate multipliers give the position domains and PVM. Fourier translation gives U_te_j=e^{-itP_j}, with P_j=F2^{-1}M_{2πξ_j}F2 on {f:ξ_j F2f∈L2}. Difference quotients prove this full derivative domain; T=-P and G=-iP match the repository convention. Differential notation P=-i∂ is asserted on Schwartz. Completeness and rational density give the standard-Borel base.

items.title: Finite transitive $G$-sets recover the stabilizer-induction classification
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a finite group with the discrete topology acting transitively on a finite set $X$,
fix $x_0\in X$, put $H=\operatorname{Stab}_G(x_0)$ and identify $X$ with $G/H$.
Let $\mathcal H=\ell^2(X)$ carry the permutation representation $U$, and let
$P$ be the projection-valued measure on $X$ assigning to $E\subseteq X$ the
orthogonal projection onto the coordinate subspace $\ell^2(E)$. Then $(U,P)$
is a transitive system of imprimitivity on the finite standard Borel space $X$,
and it is unitarily equivalent to the canonical system of the trivial
representation $1_H$ of $H$; the induced representation
$\operatorname{Ind}_H^G1_H$ is the permutation representation on $G/H$, so the
finite case of Mackey's theorem reduces to the classical
stabilizer/induction classification. More generally a finite-dimensional
unitary representation of $G$ carrying a transitive system on $X$ is induced
from a unitary representation of $H$ on a fibre of dimension
$\dim(\mathcal H)/|X|$, by the general theorem.
items.strategy: The finite discrete group and base give strong continuity and a standard-Borel system. The unitary v↦F_v, F_v(g)=v(gx0), preserves the counting quotient norm and intertwines both inverse left translation and indicator PVMs with induction of 1_H. Orthogonal singleton fibres sum to H and transitivity gives equal dimension d; since x0∈X, |X|>0 and d=dim H/|X|. The general imprimitivity theorem classifies that stabilizer fibre.

items.title: Little groups for the real $ax+b$ group and its orientation-preserving subgroup
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G=\operatorname{Aff}(\mathbb R)=\mathbb R\rtimes\mathbb R^\times$,
$N$ its translation subgroup, and $K$ its dilation subgroup. Identify
$\widehat N\cong\mathbb R$ by $\chi_\lambda(x)=e^{i\lambda x}$. The dual action
is $\lambda\mapsto\lambda/k$, so the full group $K$ has two orbits, $\{0\}$ and
$\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, with stabilizers $K$ and $\{1\}$ respectively. Its
little groups are $G$ and $N$. The irreducible representations are the
one-dimensional characters $|a|^{it}\operatorname{sign}(a)^\delta$ for
$t\in\mathbb R$, $\delta\in\{0,1\}$, and one infinite-dimensional class
$\pi=\operatorname{Ind}_N^G\chi_1\cong\operatorname{Ind}_N^G\chi_{-1}$. For
the orientation-preserving group $G_0=\mathbb R\rtimes\mathbb R_{>0}$ the
nonzero dual orbits are separately $(0,\infty)$ and $(-\infty,0)$; they give
two inequivalent infinite-dimensional representations $\pi_1,\pi_{-1}$, alongside
the characters $a^{it}$. Thus
$\widehat G=(\mathbb R\times\{0,1\})\sqcup\{\pi\}$ and
$\widehat{G_0}=\mathbb R\sqcup\{\pi_1,\pi_{-1}\}$.
items.strategy: Compute the regular finite Borel orbit partitions under λ→λ/k and apply the corollary for exhaustiveness. Schur and logarithm/sign give quotient characters. The section formula gives πλ(b,a)f(k)=exp(iλb/k)f(k/a) on Haar dk/|k|. Its N spectral PVM is multiplication by 1_E(λ/k). Spectral uniqueness for commuting unitaries, then exponentials of real/imaginary self-adjoint parts, makes every commutant operator preserve this PVM. The diagonal commutant and ergodicity make it scalar, proving irreducibility; disjoint finite log intervals prove infinite dimension. R_r f(k)=f(rk) gives same-orbit equivalences, and disjoint spectral supports distinguish signs for the positive group and distinguish zero-orbit characters.
